why: THE STONE OF THIS WORLD, AS A CONTRACT. V2 is its only author; V5 consumes it
in READ-ONLY for the rock spires of the near ridge (E-V5b), and references the
id below rather than the authoring. This file is the whole of what is promised
and the whole of what may be relied on.
IT IS NOT A SHEET, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING A CONSUMER HAS TO KNOW. A sheet
of many tiles on one page is the other convention and it inverts every answer
here: bilinear filtering reaches across a tile boundary, every mip level
reaches twice as far, so a sheet needs a clamped sampler and a gutter half a
tile wide. What V2 delivers is ONE TILE THAT WRAPS. Under wrapping the texel
past the last column IS the first column, so the right gutter is nought -- and
the nought is EARNED rather than assumed: tools/guards/guard-padding.mjs
measures the field's jump at its own seam against the jump between ordinary
neighbours inside it, on both axes, every run.
AND IT IS NOT A DOWNLOAD EITHER, which is the second thing. There is no PNG
here and there is not going to be one. The tile is three octaves of wrapped
value noise over a crack field, and 512 squared of it is 93.6 ms of arithmetic
-- too long to hold a frame, which is why it is generated in the engine's
worker and posted to the page, and short enough that shipping half a megabyte
to say the same thing would be a download bought with nothing. A consumer
calls the generator named below and gets the identical bytes: the sha256 is
published here so that identical can be CHECKED and not hoped for.
WHAT IS STABLE FROM THIS DELIVERY: the path of this file, the id, the side, the
format and the meaning of the two channels, the wrap mode and the nought
gutter. Any change to one of them is a notification to the coordinator before
it lands, never a silent edit -- that is the whole of E-V5b's sequencing, and
the reason V5's spires may be textured at all before V2 is finished.
WHAT IS NOT PROMISED: how often the tile repeats in metres. That is the
MATERIAL's number and not the tile's, and the two consumers inside V2 already
disagree about it on purpose -- the wall repeats every 1.6 m because a face
carries several courses, the rocks every 0.55 m because a rock's face is one
or two cells and at 1.6 m it would read flat. V5 picks its own from the size a
spire's face has on screen, and picking it is the only fitting a consumer has
to do.
THE OCTAVES WERE RE-CUT ON 2026-09-07 AND THE BYTES CHANGED WITH THEM. This is
the notification E-V5b asks for, written where a consumer reads it. Nothing in
the stable list above moved -- path, id, side, format, channels, wrap and the
nought gutter are what they were, and the periodicity is measured every run as
before. What changed is the FIELD: it used to open at 4 cells over the tile,
which at the masonry's 1.6 m is 0.40 m and at the rocks' 0.55 m is 0.14 m, and
44% of its amplitude sat in that one octave. Measured against the day target
(R5 SS1.4), that made the wall read its BLOCK at 0.46 m where the reference
reads 0.19 -- a patch walking across the joint between two blocks and joining
them, which is the camouflage the committente saw. The octaves now open at 16
cells and run 16 / 32 / 64 with gains 0.50 / 0.30 / 0.20, so the largest thing
on the surface is under half a block at the masonry's own repeat.
WHAT IT DOES TO A CONSUMER THAT PICKED ITS OWN METRES. The field is finer, so
a surface repeating the tile every 0.55 m now carries its grain at 0.034 m
instead of 0.14 m, and one that repeats it every 6 m carries it at 0.375 m
instead of 1.5 m. Nobody has to change anything; whoever wants the old feature
size back gets it by winding their own metresPerTile out, which is the number
this contract has always said is theirs. V5's spires are read-only consumers
and were not re-fitted by V2: the coordinator is told, and the refit is theirs
to take or to decline.
consumers: V2, the masonry of the six blocks, the stair and the platform
V5, the rock spires of the near ridge -- read-only, E-V5b

channels.r: the mottling of the stone, nought to one over the byte
channels.g: the same field read as a HEIGHT: on this stone the pale grain stands proud and the crack is the hollow, so one field answers both questions and a second fetch a step up-sun is a slope

gutterWhy: under a wrapping sampler the texel past the last column IS the first column, so a gutter would BE the seam it is meant to prevent. Earned every run by guard-padding, not assumed.

generated.wrappedBy: stoneTile(data, side) -- src/world/voxel/masonry.js, which is where the sampler settings above are declared
generated.pure: the generator imports no three.js and no DOM: it runs in the worker, on the page and under plain node from one source, which is what lets this contract be checked offline
generated.why: measured, and the reason the generating is done in the engine's worker rather than on the thread the walker is on

statistics.why: published so a consumer that gets different bytes finds out from a number rather than from a screenshot

metresPerTile.why: NOT part of the contract. Listed because a consumer choosing its own is easier with two worked examples than with none.
